clue.text: It can be produced by sulphur and fish

definitions.text: It can be produced by sulphur and fish

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
a tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: A chemistry-and-kitchen observation about what sulphur and fish give off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: sulphur compounds and fish both smell, and S plus TENCH spells the smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A foul smell is what rotten eggs (sulphur) and stale fish are known for giving off.

clue.text: Popular point of view, for example

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a stance is a position or point of view

explanation.surface: A remark citing a widely held opinion as an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: A single case cited to illustrate something is an example of it.

clue.text: As unexciting as television used to be

definitions.meaning: early television pictures were black and white, without hue

explanation.surface: A grumble that something is as dull as old TV.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'As' is a link; early TV had no colour, giving the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull lacks vividness, and old black-and-white sets literally showed no hues.

clue.text: Frenzied state of a beast of burden out East

indicators.note: out says the following letter is removed from the donkey word

parts.note: moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: A pack animal in the Orient running wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Moke is informal British slang for a donkey, a beast of burden; 'out' tells you to drop the East from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To run wild in an uncontrolled frenzy is to run in this way, a word from Malay.

clue.text: Putting opponent in tricky position, king sooner in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of these two words are disordered

explanation.surface: A snooker player hampering a rival, with a chess king hastening into danger.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, leaving the cue ball where the opponent cannot hit the target ball directly is this tactic.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving a rival with no direct shot in snooker is the source of the general sense of thwarting someone.

clue.text: A doctor's oracular verses

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor, and the 's supplies S

explanation.surface: A physician's prophetic poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: MO (medical officer) is a common crossword doctor; the possessive's S is kept here.
explanation.definitionFit: This Old Testament book records a prophet's sayings, so it is a set of prophetic verses.

clue.text: One was attractive as saint

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
drew means attracted, past tense

explanation.surface: Someone once charming who became a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Andrew is the patron saint of Scotland.

clue.text: Number of rules for making an epic movie

parts.note: ten is a number
commandments are rules or orders

explanation.surface: A recipe of rules for producing a big film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for making an' links wordplay to definition; the 1956 Cecil B DeMille epic is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cecil B DeMille's 1956 biblical spectacular about Moses is a famous Hollywood epic film.

clue.text: Pierced by weapon, moved quickly to grab attention

indicators.note: to grab means one piece takes hold of another, enclosing it

parts.note: sped means went fast
ear means attention, as in 'lend an ear'

explanation.surface: A rushed figure stabbed while seeking notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Being run through with a spear is being stabbed by that weapon.

clue.text: Form business contacts in broadcasting system

definitions.meaning: to mingle and build professional connections
a group of linked radio or TV stations

explanation.surface: Making contacts while working in TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked stations form a broadcasting chain, and the verb means making professional connections.

clue.text: Unusually verbose comment

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the next word appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A long-winded remark that is out of character.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark on something is to note it aloud as an observation, a verb sense of 'comment'.

clue.text: Wicket falls after century, then a run finishes off epic struggle England lost

indicators.note: falls after places the wicket letter following the century

parts.note: a century is a hundred years
W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: a wicket after a hundred, then a run ends a long match England lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'century' looks like a cricket score of 100 but is a hundred years; 'then' and 'finishes off' are links. The conflict of 1337-1453 between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: England fought France for over a century in the late Middle Ages and lost almost all its French lands.

clue.text: Turn off old record including fashionable piece of song

indicators.note: including means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record, now dated
in means fashionable
a line is a single part of a song's lyrics

explanation.surface: Switching off an old vinyl that features a trendy snatch of music.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone off doing something is to make them unwilling, a transitive sense of the verb.

clue.text: Moved from Exeter, say, and spent time in the country

definitions.meaning: temporarily sent away from a university, Exeter being an example

explanation.surface: Someone sent away from an English city who then lived rurally.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter is a UK university; a student suspended from one has been sent down for a period.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both suspended from university as a punishment and retired to rural life.

clue.text: Some language lessons lasting a long time

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that certain foreign-language classes go on endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless never seems to grow old, so it endures.

clue.text: All for nothing, for example

parts.note: read as a word pairing, everything set against its opposite none, an example of a word paired with its opposite

explanation.surface: Wasted effort, like all for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A word opposite in meaning to another is this, as all is to nothing.

clue.text: One new short drink I had, lacking flavour

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a sip is a small taste of a drink
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a quick, tasteless drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is bland or tasteless is said to be this.

clue.text: Odd pictures — one contained dozens of blackbirds

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of the next word are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: Strange pictures of a pie stuffed with birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Sing a Song of Sixpence' has four and twenty blackbirds baked in a pie: two dozen.
explanation.definitionFit: The pastry shell of the rhyme's pie enclosed the twenty-four birds.

clue.text: More than a grand classic

definitions.meaning: a guinea was 21 shillings, so a thousand of them is more than a thousand pounds
one of the five English flat-racing Classics, run at Newmarket

explanation.surface: Something worth over a thousand that is also timeless.
explanation.walkthrough: A guinea was an old British coin worth one pound and one shilling; a 'grand' is a thousand pounds. The race of that name is one of Britain's Classics.
explanation.definitionFit: The fillies' race at Newmarket is one of the Classics, and the sum literally exceeds a thousand pounds.

clue.text: One English novelist or another cut

indicators.note: cut says the final letter is chopped from the second novelist's name

parts.note: another English novelist, H G Wells

explanation.surface: A choice between two English writers, one trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points to a second English novelist, Wells, whose last letter is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Blair wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four under this pen name.

clue.text: Most reasonable form of assent

indicators.note: form of says the letters of the next word are reshaped

explanation.surface: The most sensible way of saying yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Most rational or sound of mind is the superlative of 'sensible' in this sense.

clue.text: Policy for economic revival that follows a reshuffle?

definitions.meaning: Franklin Roosevelt's 1930s programme to recover from the Depression
after the cards are shuffled again, they are dealt out afresh

explanation.surface: A government programme that comes after a cabinet shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshuffle' suggests a cabinet change but refers to shuffling cards before dealing; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt's recovery programme bore this name, and a fresh deal of cards comes after shuffling.

clue.text: Something bad, as it happens, turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: live means broadcast in real time, as it happens

explanation.surface: Something nasty that appeared live on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness or harm is something bad, a noun sense.

clue.text: Annoyance of king following three in succession

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Annoyance of king following three in succession', gives GR (king) and CHAIN (succession) but 'three' has no job; likely OCR damage and no scan or blog confirms the wording
annotationWithheld.clue: Annoyance of king following three in succession

clue.text: The second man one put in prison

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: can is slang for a prison
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Another man jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Adam was the first man and his son Cain the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's firstborn son is the second male human in the biblical account.

clue.text: Rich characters, female, one found in play by Shaw

definitions.text: one found in play by Shaw
definitions.meaning: Shaw's 1936 comedy is titled after such a wealthy woman, singular

explanation.surface: Wealthy women, one of whom appears in a Shaw comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: George Bernard Shaw's play 'The Millionairess' gives the second sense, though it names only one such woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Women with fortunes over a million are wealthy women, and Shaw's title character is one.
